geography: City and County of San Francisco
scopeNote: A measurement contract for evaluating local giving opportunities. It is not a ranking of organizations and contains no inferred cost-effectiveness, QALY, or WELLBY estimate.

classificationRules.outcome: A change in a person's condition or durable status, measured against a pre-specified follow-up window.
classificationRules.proxy: An administrative measure associated with the desired outcome but insufficient by itself to establish that outcome.
classificationRules.output: A delivered service, contact, placement, distribution, or enrollment; outputs are not outcomes.
classificationRules.counterfactual: A donor-attributable effect requires a credible comparison or a transparent model. Before that, the ontology reports observed change only.
classificationRules.equity: Every measure should be disaggregated where privacy and sample size permit; aggregate improvement cannot hide a widening subgroup gap.
classificationRules.conversion: QALY and WELLBY translation is blocked until a versioned local model states population, baseline, duration, displacement, deadweight, uncertainty, and source evidence.

outcomes.label: Housing stability
outcomes.question: Did a household remain in permanent housing rather than return to homelessness?
outcomes.observableMeasure: People exiting to permanent housing who remain housed without a recorded return to homelessness at 6, 12, and 24 months.
outcomes.unitSemantics: Report both the retained count and rate by follow-up window. Person-years require observed duration; a placement is not one person-year.
outcomes.population: San Francisco residents receiving prevention, rapid-rehousing, or permanent-housing support
outcomes.timeWindow: 6, 12, and 24 months after assistance or permanent-housing exit
administrativeProxies: housing retention recorded in ONE System
return to homelessness within two years
blockedClaims: placements equal stable housing
all observed retention was caused by the donor
housing units equal unique people housed

outcomes.label: Unsheltered days avoided
outcomes.question: How much time outside was prevented or shortened?
outcomes.observableMeasure: Modeled difference between observed unsheltered days and a credible no-program counterfactual for the same target population.
outcomes.unitSemantics: One person-day is one person unsheltered for one day. PIT counts are snapshots and cannot be multiplied into annual person-days without a duration model.
outcomes.population: People experiencing or at imminent risk of unsheltered homelessness in San Francisco
outcomes.timeWindow: Program entry through 12 months, with sensitivity through 24 months
administrativeProxies: first and last observed homeless dates
allowedClaims: observed days recorded outside or in shelter
modeled days avoided with assumptions and interval
blockedClaims: PIT reduction equals donor impact
each shelter night is an unsheltered day avoided
the plan's modeled 300-day adult duration is an observed person-level value

outcomes.label: Overdose deaths averted
outcomes.question: Did the intervention reduce accidental overdose mortality?
outcomes.observableMeasure: Difference in certified accidental overdose deaths between the intervention population and a credible comparison or modeled counterfactual.
outcomes.unitSemantics: Observed deaths are counts; deaths averted are counterfactual estimates. Naloxone reversals, kits, and treatment starts remain separate measures.
outcomes.population: People at risk of fatal overdose in San Francisco
outcomes.timeWindow: Monthly surveillance; program evaluation at 6 and 12 months
allowedClaims: modeled deaths averted with design and uncertainty
blockedClaims: each naloxone reversal equals one death averted
kits distributed equal reversals
preliminary deaths equal final death-certificate totals

outcomes.label: Mental-health stabilization
outcomes.question: Did functioning improve while crisis and urgent-care use fell?
outcomes.canonicalUnit: participants meeting a pre-specified clinical and functional stabilization threshold
outcomes.observableMeasure: Participants with reliable improvement on a named functioning or quality-of-life instrument and no unplanned urgent/emergent behavioral-health use during follow-up.
outcomes.unitSemantics: Name the instrument, threshold, baseline severity, and follow-up. Routine-care engagement alone is not stabilization.
outcomes.population: San Francisco behavioral-health participants, with Mental Health SF target population reported separately
outcomes.timeWindow: 90 and 180 days after intake or crisis discharge
allowedClaims: share meeting the pre-specified stabilization threshold
blockedClaims: appointment attendance equals stabilization
fewer encounters always means improved health
housing placement alone equals clinical improvement

outcomes.label: Food security
outcomes.question: Did a household gain reliable access to adequate food?
outcomes.canonicalUnit: household-months at a named USDA food-security level
outcomes.observableMeasure: Households moving from low or very low food security to food secure on the same validated survey module, with duration measured at follow-up.
outcomes.unitSemantics: Report households and household-months separately. Survey instruments, recall periods, and sampled populations must match before aggregation.
outcomes.population: San Francisco households served, with low-income, unhoused, student, and birthing populations reported separately
outcomes.timeWindow: Baseline, 30 days, 6 months, and 12 months using a consistent recall period
allowedClaims: meals or benefits delivered as outputs
blockedClaims: one meal equals one day food secure
different prevalence samples can be pooled
benefit enrollment proves food security

outcomes.label: Educational attainment
outcomes.question: Did a student attain a defined learning, credit, credential, or persistence milestone?
outcomes.canonicalUnit: students attaining one named educational milestone
outcomes.observableMeasure: Students reaching a pre-specified milestone—such as expected learning growth, on-track credits, graduation, A–G completion, college enrollment, or persistence—within its proper cohort.
outcomes.unitSemantics: Each milestone is a separate outcome. Test-score growth, credits, graduation, and postsecondary persistence must never be summed into one attainment count.
outcomes.population: SFUSD students or a clearly defined San Francisco learner cohort
outcomes.timeWindow: School year for learning and credits; four-year cohort for graduation; 12-month follow-up for postsecondary enrollment
allowedClaims: modeled incremental attainment with design and uncertainty
blockedClaims: enrollment equals learning
all graduates were caused by the program
different milestones are interchangeable
suppressed cells equal zero

outcomes.label: Violence reduction
outcomes.question: Were violent injuries prevented without displacement to another place or population?
outcomes.canonicalUnit: assault-related injuries averted, reported separately by severity
outcomes.observableMeasure: Difference in assault-related emergency visits, hospitalizations, or deaths between the intervention population or geography and a credible comparison.
outcomes.unitSemantics: Fatal, hospitalized, emergency-treated, and police-reported events are separate measures. Averted injuries require a counterfactual and displacement check.
outcomes.population: San Francisco residents and people present in the intervention geography
allowedClaims: estimated injuries averted with design and interval
blockedClaims: calls for service equal victimizations
a local decline proves program attribution
hospitalizations represent all violence
events displaced nearby count as prevented

outcomes.label: Economic mobility
outcomes.question: Did earnings and sustained employment improve after program exit?
outcomes.canonicalUnit: participants in unsubsidized employment in the fourth quarter after exit
outcomes.observableMeasure: Employment in the second and fourth quarters after exit and median earnings in the second quarter, reported as separate WIOA-aligned outcomes.
outcomes.unitSemantics: Employment counts/rates and earnings distributions are not additive. A job placement at exit is an early proxy, not sustained mobility.
outcomes.population: San Francisco workforce-program participants, with eligibility and barriers to employment explicit
outcomes.timeWindow: Second and fourth quarters after exit; longer follow-up when wage records permit
allowedClaims: estimated earnings gain with design and uncertainty
blockedClaims: training completion equals employment
initial placement equals Q4 retention
median earnings can be multiplied by participant count
observed wages are all caused by the program

overlaps.risk: The same housing placement may improve both outcomes.
overlaps.rule: Report both measures but never sum people housed and days avoided; preserve one participant and episode identity.

overlaps.risk: Supportive housing can affect housing and clinical outcomes.
overlaps.rule: Attribute each outcome through its own measurement model; do not treat housing placement as clinical stabilization.

overlaps.risk: Substance-use treatment and crisis care may affect both mortality and stabilization.
overlaps.rule: Keep treatment starts as outputs; model mortality and clinical outcomes separately.

overlaps.risk: Cash, benefits, and employment may affect both food access and income.
overlaps.rule: Measure household food security and labor outcomes separately; do not count benefit value as earnings.

overlaps.risk: Education may affect later employment and earnings.
overlaps.rule: Do not book future earnings alongside attainment unless a longitudinal model separates timing, deadweight, and persistence.

overlaps.risk: Community programs may jointly affect trauma exposure and behavioral health.
overlaps.rule: Keep injury events and clinical functioning as distinct outcomes; deduplicate participants only within each measure.
